purpose: Every value a page relies on, checked against the primary source that sets it. scripts/apply_primary_sources.py applies the corrections below to the extracted dataset, checks every expected value, and marks a jurisdiction verified only when all of them match. extract_tax_data.py runs it after every extraction, so a regeneration cannot undo a correction.

pennsylvania.why: Adds the employee unemployment-compensation withholding (0.07% of all wages) that every Pennsylvania paycheck carries.

sources.title: Georgia DOR, 2026 Employer's Withholding Tax Guide (revised June 2026): HB 463, retroactive to January 1, 2026 — flat 4.99%; standard deduction $30,000 married filing jointly, $15,000 single, head of household and married filing separately

withholdingTransition.note: HB 463 cut the 2026 rate to 4.99% retroactively; employers withheld 5.19% until May 11, 2026.

dependentAllowance.source: Georgia 2026 Employer's Withholding Tax Guide: HB 463 raised the dependent deduction from $4,000 to $5,000, retroactive to January 1, 2026

georgia.why: Records the mid-year withholding change, and adds the $5,000 dependent deduction.

sources.title: Illinois DOR Informational Bulletin FY 2026-15: "The 2025 personal exemption amount is $2,850"; "The personal exemption amount for tax year 2026 will increase to $2,925"; not allowed above $250,000 AGI ($500,000 joint)
IL-700-T 2026: "The income tax rate is 4.95 percent and the exemption allowance is $2,925"
2025 Schedule IL-E/EITC: "Multiply the total number of dependents you are claiming by $2,850"

dependentAllowance.source: Schedule IL-E/EITC: dependents at the exemption amount ($2,850 for 2025; $2,925 for 2026 per Bulletin FY 2026-15); not allowed above $250,000 AGI ($500,000 joint)

notes: The 2026 personal exemption is $2,925 ($5,850 on a joint return) and is not allowed above $250,000 of AGI ($500,000 joint) (Informational Bulletin FY 2026-15).
The 4.95% rate has applied since July 1, 2017.

illinois.why: The extracted exemption ($2,850) was the 2025 amount, carried forward because upstream had not indexed it; a joint return claims two exemptions. Adds dependents at the exemption amount.

sources.title: Md. Code, Tax-General section 10-105(a): State rates and brackets
Md. Code, Tax-General section 10-217: $3,350 / $6,700 for 2025, indexed from 2026 by the IRC 1(f)(3) cost-of-living adjustment (2024 base), each increase rounded down to a multiple of $50
Comptroller of Maryland, 2026 Employer Withholding Guide and Form MW507 (2026): standard deduction $3,400; exemption $3,200 with the AGI phase-down table
BLS chained CPI-U (SUUR0000SA0), 12-month averages to August 2024 and August 2025, via FRED

dependentAllowance.source: Form MW507 (2026): each exemption, dependents included, is worth $3,200 and steps down with federal AGI

notes: The 2026 standard deduction is $3,400 ($6,850 joint and head of household), indexed from 2026 (Tax-General section 10-217).
The current brackets took effect on January 1, 2025.

maryland.why: The extracted amounts ($3,350/$6,700) were 2025's. $3,400 is published by the Comptroller. The Comptroller has not yet published the joint/head-of-household figure; $6,850 is section 10-217(c) applied to BLS data (C-CPI-U 177.206 / 173.016 = +2.42%; $6,700 x 2.42% = $162 -> rounded down to $150), and the same formula reproduces the published $3,400 ($81 -> $50). Recheck against the 2026 resident booklet when it is released. Adds dependents at the same $3,200 exemption value. A joint return claims two personal exemptions (MW507: 'Multiply the number of your personal exemptions by the value of each exemption'); the extracted data gave a married couple one.

sources.title: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Hall Income Tax: the tax on interest and dividends was phased out and is fully repealed for tax years beginning January 1, 2021; it never applied to salaries or wages
Tenn. Const. art. II, sec. 28 (amended November 4, 2014): the legislature shall not levy, authorize or otherwise permit any state or local tax upon payroll or earned personal income
Code of Virginia section 58.1-320: 2% to $3,000, 3% to $5,000, 5% to $17,000, 5.75% above, for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 1990

Code of Virginia section 58.1-322.03: standard deduction $8,750 single and $17,500 married (half each on separate returns) for taxable years 2025 and 2026; $930 for each personal exemption allowable for federal purposes
Virginia Tax, Deductions: Single $8,750; Married filing jointly $17,500; Married filing separately $8,750
Virginia Tax, Exemptions: $930 for yourself, your spouse and each dependent

dependentAllowance.source: Code of Virginia section 58.1-322.03(2)(a): $930 for each personal exemption allowable for federal purposes, dependents included

notes: Virginia has no head-of-household status; a head of household files as single and takes the $8,750 standard deduction.
The standard deduction is $8,750 ($17,500 married) for 2025 and 2026 and rises to $9,200 ($18,400) in 2027 (Code of Virginia section 58.1-322.03).
The four brackets have been unchanged since 1990.

virginia.why: Adds the standard deduction ($8,750 / $17,500), the $930 personal exemption (two on a joint return) and $930 for each dependent; none were in the extracted record.

sources.title: Michigan Department of Treasury, Withholding Tax Information by Calendar Year: 2026 rate 4.25%, personal exemption $5,900 (2025: 4.25%, $5,800)

dependentAllowance.source: Michigan Treasury: the $5,900 personal exemption is claimed for the filer, a spouse and each dependent

notes: The 2026 rate is 4.25% and the personal exemption is $5,900 for the filer, a spouse and each dependent (Michigan Treasury).
Michigan has no standard deduction for wage earners under the retirement-age rules.

michigan.why: Adds the 2026 personal exemption ($5,900, two on a joint return) and $5,900 for each dependent; none were in the extracted record.

sources.title: Indiana Department of Revenue, Departmental Notice #1 (effective October 1, 2026): "For 2026, the state adjusted gross income tax rate for individuals is 2.95%"; $1,000 per personal exemption; $1,500 per additional dependent exemption

dependentAllowance.source: Departmental Notice #1: $1,000 per exemption, dependents included, and a further $1,500 for each qualifying dependent child

notes: Every Indiana county adds its own income tax on top of the state rate; it depends on the county you live in on January 1.

countyIncomeTax.basis: The county rate applies to the same base as the state tax: wages less the exemptions. Marion County on a $95,000 salary, single: (95,000 - 1,000) x 2.02% = 1,898.80.
countyIncomeTax.source: Indiana Department of Revenue, Departmental Notice #1, county tax rates effective October 1, 2026; a resident pays the rate of the county they live in on January 1

indiana.why: Adds the $1,000 personal exemption (two on a joint return), $1,000 for each dependent and the further $1,500 for each dependent child; none were in the extracted record.
